newsitem.title: UK: UK May oil output hits 2-yr low due field shutdown.
newsitem.headline: UK May oil output hits 2-yr low due field shutdown.

text.p: U.K. oil output fell by 9.2 percent in May, its sixth successive monthly fall, the Royal Bank of Scotland said.
Output of 2.28 million barrels per day (bpd) was its lowest level since June 1995, it said.
Gas production also experienced its normal seasonal decline reflecting lower summer demand and resulting in a reduction of 14.4 percent in combined oil and gas production.

U.K. oil and gas revenues in May fell sharply reflecting the drop in oil output and continued strength of the pound. Revenues declined by 9.5 percent in the month and were also 7.5 percent lower than a year ago.
Stephen Boyle, head of business economics at the bank, said that concern over the six-month decline in oil production was probably premature.

"For most of this year oil production has remained ahead of the level achieved in 1996. There was a significant decline in May but that probably reflects slightly earlier shutdowns on some platforms for summer maintenance and delays in bringing new fields on stream", he said.
Boyle said June's OPEC meeting had not introduced any new system for controlling over-production by its members.

"While there is strong rhetorical support for the quotas, experience suggests the reality will be continued over-production. If this happens there is no immediate prospect of a squeeze on supply and prices should continue to trade either side of $18 (a barrel)."
